newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh, India agree not to shelter "terrorists".
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh, India agree not to shelter "terrorists".

text.p: Bangladesh and India have agreed not to give shelter to "terrorists", including insurgents operating across their borders, the Daily Star reported on Wednesday.
It said the decision was reached at a five-day border conference in New Delhi that ended on April 12.

At the conference, Bangladesh proposed the eviction of tribal Shanti Bahini guerrillas from the Chittagong Hill Tracts who are now living in camps in India's northeastern state of Tripura, the newspaper, quoting unidentified officials, said. Bangladesh said the "terrorists" should be driven away. The Shanti Bahini have been fighting since 1973 for autonomy in the Hill Tracts, which border India and Burma.
India also sought Dhaka's cooperation to prevent Indian "terrorists" from using Bangladesh as a base to conduct insurgency in northeastern states, the newspaper said.
"Bangladesh and India have agreed not to give shelter to other country's terrorists, like cross-border insurgents, in their respective lands," the Star said, quoting officials.
The two countries had in principle agreed not to shelter "terrorists" from across the borders during the visit to Dhaka earlier this year by Indian prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
India had often accused Bangladesh of harbouring insurgents fighting for separate homelands in its northeastern states.
"We are in a broad consensus to implement the decision," one senior Bangladesh official said on Wednesday, referring to the agreement reached during Deve Gowda's trip to Dhaka.
